Definition: Pul, the name of an Assyrian king and of a Libyan people
BiblicalUsage: Pul is the name of an Assyrian king, and of a distant people. Pul the king of Assyria came against the land of Israel, and Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand, and God stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and carried away the Reubenites and the Gadites. And Isaiah says the LORD will send those that escape to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Pul shows me God uses even pagan kings as His instruments: He stirred Pul's spirit to judge Israel, and He will send messengers to Pul's people to declare His glory.
